title: Journal Club: Using CRISPR to Prevent Coronavirus and Influenza Infection

reader_summary.headline: Hello, and welcome to the A16Z Journal Club.
reader_summary.overview: Hello, and welcome to the A16Z Journal Club. I'm Lauren Richardson, and today we're talking about a new approach to prevent viral infection. Specifically, we're discussing a recent article published in the journal Cell, titled Development of CRISPR as an Antiviral Strategy to Prevent SARS-V2 and Influenza.

key_points.text: Specifically, we're discussing a recent article published in the journal Cell, titled Development of CRISPR as an Antiviral Strategy to Prevent SARS-V2 and Influenza.
key_points.evidence_quote: Specifically, we're discussing a recent article published in the journal Cell, titled Development of CRISPR as an Antiviral Strategy to Prevent SARS-V2 and Influenza, from the labs of Marie LaRusa, David Lewis, and Stanley Chi at Stanford.

key_points.text: Our discussion covers the differences between this newly developed prophylactic antiviral strategy, traditional vaccines and antiviral drugs.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our discussion covers the differences between this newly developed prophylactic antiviral strategy, traditional vaccines and antiviral drugs, how it can target a huge range of viruses and the next steps needed to go from paper to practice.

key_points.text: I'm joined today by A16Z general partner, Vijay, and bioteam partner, Andy Tran.
key_points.evidence_quote: I'm joined today by A16Z general partner, Vijay, and bioteam partner, Andy Tran.

key_points.text: But before we begin, here's my summary of the article.
